title: SHARE IT Act
official_summary:
Source code Harmonization And Reuse in Information Technology Act or the SHARE IT Act

This act requires federal agencies to ensure that custom-developed code (i.e., source code that is produced under an agency contract, funded exclusively by the federal government, or developed by federal employees as part of their official duties) and certain technical components of the code such as architecture designs and metadata are (1) owned by the agency, (2) stored at no less than one public or private repository, and (3) accessible to federal employees under certain procedures. Agency contracts for custom-development of software must acquire and exercise rights sufficient to allow government-wide access, sharing, use, and modification of any custom-developed code.

The act does not apply to source code that is classified, developed primarily for use in a national security system, or developed by an element of the intelligence community. An agency's office of the chief information officer may exempt source code from being shared or made publicly accessible to protect individual privacy.

Within 120 days of enactment, the Office of Electronic Government shall establish minimum reporting standards for agencies relating to certain topics, such as measuring the frequency of reuse of code. Within one year of enactment, the Federal Acquisition Regulation must be revised to implement the act's provisions.

summary.headline: The SHARE IT Act requires federal agencies to own, store, and share custom-built software code so other agencies can reuse it.
summary.what_it_does: Federal agencies must make sure that custom code they pay for or that federal employees write is owned by the agency, stored in at least one public or private repository, and available to federal employees. Agency software contracts must secure enough rights so the code can be shared, used, and changed across the government. Classified code, code mainly for national security systems, and intelligence community code are excluded, and agencies may hold back code to protect personal privacy.

who_it_affects.how: They must store custom-developed code in a repository, make it accessible to federal employees, and report on things like how often code is reused.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that build custom software under federal contracts
who_it_affects.how: Their contracts must give the government rights to access, share, use, and modify the code they create for agencies.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees who write or use software
who_it_affects.how: They gain access to code developed by other agencies under set procedures.
They may exempt code from being shared or made public to protect individual privacy.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; reporting standards are due within 120 days, and federal contracting rules must be updated within one year.
